     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesBaseSheaf
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModulesPushforwardBaseChange
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafH0BaseChange
     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.LocalGenerators
    10	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveH0BaseChange
    11	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjectiveSite
    12	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0EndgameContract
    13	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RingDatumEngine
    14	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisorsClass
    15	
    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/
    37	
    38	set_option autoImplicit false
    39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    40	
    41	universe u
    42	
    43	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    44	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    45	
    46	open scoped TensorProduct
    47	
    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    49	
    50	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    51	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    52	
    53	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    54	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    55	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    58	
    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    72	  datum_class :
    73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
    80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
    87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    90	  h0_rank_one :
    91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1
    93	
    94	namespace PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    95	
    96	variable {pi} {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}
    97	
    98	noncomputable local instance presentationModuleSections
    99	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) (U : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens) :
   100	    Module P.cover.Carrier Γ(P.module, U) :=
   101	  Scheme.moduleKSections
   102	    (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module U
   103	
   104	/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.
   105	
   106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
   107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   109	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   110	    B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] (Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) ≃ₗ[B]
   111	      Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   112	  P.datum.datumH0BaseChange B
   113	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing)
   114	
   115	/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
   116	noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   117	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   119	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   120	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ⟶
   121	      P.module :=
   122	  (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   123	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module
   124	
   125	/-! ## Native pushforward base change and evaluation coherence -/
   126	
   127	/-- The canonical native pushforward base-change isomorphism supplied by the presentation.
   128	
   129	The isomorphism is not chosen independently: its hom is definitionally
   130	`(canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module`. -/
   131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   135	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   136	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   137	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj
   138	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   139	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   140	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) := by
   141	  exact @asIso _ _ _ _ ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module)
   142	    (P.native_pushforward_base_change g f' g' sq)
   143	
   144	/-- The native pushforward base-change isomorphism for an affine coefficient extension. -/
   145	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIsoAffine (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   146	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   147	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   148	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   149	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier B)))).obj
   150	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   151	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   152	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   153	        (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))).obj
   154	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)).obj P.module) :=
   155	  P.nativeBaseChangeIso
   156	    (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B).left
   157	    (snd C (overSpec k B)).left
   158	    (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)
   159	    (Over.isPullback_whiskerLeft C (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B))
   160	
   161	/-- The source of evaluation identifies canonically with the source of evaluation after any
   162	cartesian base change. -/

    14	This module is the first divisor consumer of PicRankOneLocalPresentation.  The projective

    10	# DAT-B B-1 — the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop to `h⁰ = 1`
    11	
    12	The coverage-side normalization of the DAT-B worksheet (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
    13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage
    14	argument), given an **admissible point oracle** `P` — a set of closed `K`-rational points
    15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
    16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
    17	
    18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
    19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).
    20	
    21	The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5, worksheet §1.2 step 5) consumes this with
    22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
    23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
    24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.
    25	
    26	## Route (worksheet §1.4, per step for the current `W'` with `h¹ = 0`, `deg = g + e'`)
    27	
    28	* **The bad locus is small** (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`): `H⁰(𝒪(W'))` is nonzero
    29	  (rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`), its base divisor
    30	  (`Scheme.baseDivisor`, the DD-F kit) has finite support consisting of closed points, so
    31	  the non-base locus contains a nonempty open (complement of a finite closed set in the
    32	  irreducible curve — it contains the generic point) and the oracle supplies an admissible
    33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
    34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
    35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
    36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
    37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`
    38	  (`Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt` through the `h⁰` bridge
    39	  `finrank_divisorSections_top`) — while the χ-ledger (`chi_divisorSheaf`) with
    40	  `residueDeg x = 1` and `h¹(𝒪(W')) = 0` gives `χ(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1`; equality
    41	  forces BOTH `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` AND `h¹(𝒪(W' − x)) = 0` — the induction
    42	  invariant.
    43	* **Terminate at `e' = 0`**: `h⁰ = 1` by the rank anchor at `deg = g`, `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`.
    44	
    45	The strict-drop precedents `h0_normalization_sub_single_lt` (`PFib.lean`) and
    46	`h0_window_sub_single_lt` (`CarveDegreePinch.lean`) are window-specific mirrors of the
    47	drop step (worksheet risk 3 mitigation); their `deg_single`/`coeffAt` bookkeeping is
    48	imitated, not consumed.  Pure field level — no scheme beyond the fibre curve appears
    49	(the DD-F discipline).  The genus enters only through `hχ : χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`; the
    50	worksheet's standing `h⁰(𝒪_Y) = 1` is not needed by this brick and is not threaded.
    51	-/

    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace

    61	
    62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    63	
    64	open Scheme
    65	
    66	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    67	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    69	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    70	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    71	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    72	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    73	
    74	/-! ## The bad locus is small: an admissible non-base point -/
    75	
    76	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    77	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
    78	/-- **An admissible non-base point** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 1): if `H⁰(𝒪(W))` is nonzero
    79	and `P` is dense (meets every nonempty open) and consists of closed points, then some
    80	`x ∈ P` is *not* a base point of the system: some nonzero section `f ∈ H⁰(𝒪(W))` has
    81	exact order at `x`, `(W + div f)ₓ = 0`.  The base locus is contained in the support of
    82	the base divisor `bd(H⁰(𝒪(W)))` — a finite set of closed points, whose complement is a
    83	nonempty open (it contains the generic point); the base-divisor achiever
    84	(`Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
    85	outside the support. -/
    86	theorem exists_admissible_nonbase_point (P : Set Y)
    87	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    88	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    89	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W)) :
    90	    ∃ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (_ : x ∈ P) (f : Y.functionField)
    91	      (_ : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0),
    92	      coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
    93	        = 0 := by
    94	  classical
    95	  set T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K W ⊤ with hT
    96	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 := by
    97	    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
    98	    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=
    99	      finrank_divisorSections_top K W
   100	    rw [hbot, finrank_bot] at hfr
   101	    omega
   102	  set B : Y.CurveDivisor := Scheme.baseDivisor K T W hTne with hB
   103	  -- the support of the base divisor is a finite set of closed points
   104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=
   105	    isClosed_biUnion_finset (fun p _ =>
   106	      isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2)
   107	  set U : Y.Opens :=
   108	    ⟨(⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y))ᶜ, hclosed.isOpen_compl⟩ with hU
   109	  have hUne : (U : Set Y).Nonempty := by
   110	    refine ⟨genericPoint Y, fun hmem => ?_⟩
   111	    obtain ⟨p, _, hp⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp hmem
   112	    exact p.2 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hp).symm
   113	  obtain ⟨x, hxP, hxU⟩ := hdense U hUne
   114	  have hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y := hPcl x hxP
   115	  -- outside the support the base multiplicity vanishes
   116	  have hxc : x ∉ ⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y) := hxU
   117	  have hxB : coeffAt hx B = 0 := by
   118	    by_contra hne
   119	    exact hxc (Set.mem_iUnion₂.mpr
   120	      ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hne, rfl⟩)
   121	  have hBat : (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T W ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) = 0 := by
   122	    rw [← Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hTne hx]
   123	    exact hxB
   124	  -- the achiever realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
   125	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, hach⟩ :=
   126	    Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K (le_refl T) hTne hx
   127	  exact ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfT, hf, hach.trans hBat⟩
   128	
   129	/-! ## The exact drop at a rational non-base point -/
   130	
   131	/-- **The exact drop** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 2): at a closed `K`-rational point `x`
   132	(`residueDeg x = 1`) that is not a base point of `H⁰(𝒪(W))` — witnessed by a nonzero
   133	section `f` of exact order at `x` — and under `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`,
   134	
   135	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − x)) + 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W))`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − x)) = 0`.
   136	
   137	`≤`: sections of `W − x` are sections of `W` vanishing one order deeper at `x`, a proper
   138	subspace since `f` violates the deeper bound — one linear condition as `residueDeg x = 1`.
   139	`≥`: the χ-ledger gives `χ(𝒪(W − x)) = χ(𝒪(W)) − 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W)) − 1` and `h¹ ≥ 0`.
   140	Equality forces both conclusions — the induction invariant of the greedy drop. -/
   141	theorem h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase (W : Y.CurveDivisor)
   142	    (h1W : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
   143	    {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hdx : Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   144	    {f : Y.functionField} (hfW : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0)
   145	    (hnb : coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
   146	      = 0) :
   147	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + 1
   148	        = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) ∧
   149	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   150	  -- sections of `W − x` sit inside sections of `W` …
   151	  have hle : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   152	      ≤ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   153	    refine divisorSections_mono K ?_ ⊤
   154	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   155	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
   156	    by_cases hyx : y = x
   157	    · subst hyx
   158	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   159	      omega
   160	    · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   161	      omega
   162	  -- … properly: the exact-order section violates the deeper bound at `x`
   163	  have hfnot : f ∉ divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤ := by
   164	    intro hmem
   165	    have h0le := (mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf).mp hmem
   166	    have hcoeff := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp h0le x hx
   167	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   168	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self] at hcoeff
   169	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hnb
   170	    omega
   171	  have hne : divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤
   172	      ≠ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   173	    intro heq
   174	    rw [← heq] at hfW
   175	    exact hfnot hfW
   176	  have hdrop : Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   177	      < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   178	    have hlt := Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_ne hle hne)
   179	    rwa [finrank_divisorSections_top K _, finrank_divisorSections_top K _] at hlt
   180	  -- the χ-ledger on both levels
   181	  have hchiW := chi_divisorSheaf K W
   182	  have hchiWx := chi_divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   183	  have hdegsub : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   184	      = CurveDivisor.deg K W - 1 := by
   185	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1, hdx,
   186	      Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   187	  rw [hdegsub] at hchiWx
   188	  have hh0W : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K W) = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) : ℤ) :=
   189	    Sheaf.chi_eq_h0 h1W
   190	  have hchidef : Sheaf.chi (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   191	      = (Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ)
   192	        - (Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) : ℤ) := rfl
   193	  have hh1 : Sheaf.h1 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) = 0 := by omega
   194	  refine ⟨by omega, ?_⟩
   195	  haveI := moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   196	  exact Module.finrank_zero_iff.mp hh1
   197	
   198	/-! ## The keystone: the greedy drop to `h⁰ = 1` -/
   199	
   200	/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):
   201	on the curve bundle `Y` over the field `K` with `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`, let `P` be an
   202	admissible point oracle — closed points, `K`-rational (`residueDeg = 1`), dense (meeting
   203	every nonempty open).  Then every divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`
   204	admits an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
   205	
   206	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`.
   207	
   208	Induction on `e`: at each step the rank anchor gives `h⁰ = e' + 1 ≥ 1`, the oracle
   209	supplies a rational non-base point (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`), and the exact
   210	drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while
   211	lowering the degree budget by one.  The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5) instantiates
   212	`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
   213	theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
   214	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   215	    (P : Set Y)
   216	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   217	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
   218	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   219	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (e : ℕ)
   220	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e)
   221	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   222	    ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   223	      (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   224	      Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   225	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) := by
   226	  suffices H : ∀ (e : ℕ) (W : Y.CurveDivisor),
   227	      CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e →
   228	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →
   229	      ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   230	        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   231	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   232	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
   233	    H e W hdeg h1
   234	  intro e
   235	  induction e with
   236	  | zero =>
   237	    intro W hdeg h1
   238	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   239	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   240	    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   241	    · intro x hx hne
   242	      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
   243	    · rw [sub_zero]
   244	      push_cast at hanchor
   245	      omega
   246	    · rw [sub_zero]
   247	      exact h1
   248	  | succ e ih =>
   249	    intro W hdeg h1
   250	    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
   251	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   252	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   253	    have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   254	      push_cast at hanchor
   255	      omega
   256	    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
   257	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
   258	      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos
   259	    obtain ⟨hdrop, h1'⟩ :=
   260	      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
   261	    have hdeg' : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = (g : ℤ) + e := by
   262	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   263	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one, hdeg]
   264	      push_cast
   265	      ring
   266	    obtain ⟨S', hS'0, hS'deg, hS'P, hS'h0, hS'h1⟩ :=
   267	      ih (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) hdeg' h1'
   268	    have hsplit : W - (S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   269	        = W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - S' := by
   270	      abel
   271	    refine ⟨S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   272	    · -- effectivity
   273	      refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   274	      have h0S' := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hS'0 y hy
   275	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h0S'
   276	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   277	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   278	      · subst hyx
   279	        rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   280	        omega
   281	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   282	        omega
   283	    · -- degree
   284	      rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, hS'deg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   285	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   286	      push_cast
   287	      ring
   288	    · -- support in `P`
   289	      intro y hy hne
   290	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hne
   291	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   292	      · subst hyx
   293	        exact hxP
   294	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx, add_zero] at hne
   295	        exact hS'P y hy hne
   296	    · rw [hsplit]
   297	      exact hS'h0
   298	    · rw [hsplit]
   299	      exact hS'h1
   300	
   301	end AlgebraicGeometry

     8	/-!
     9	# DD-0 — the section bound `h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)`
    10	
    11	The section-bound half of the DAT-D brick DD-0 (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §5 DD-0,
    12	consumed by the P-fib normalization step F1 of §3.3): on the curve bundle `X` (integral,
    13	smooth of relative dimension one, quasi-compact over a field `K`, with finite `H⁰`/`H¹`
    14	of `𝒪_X`), the global-section count of any divisor sheaf is bounded by its degree,
    15	
    16	`h⁰(𝒪(A)) ≤ max 0 (deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X))`,
    17	
    18	hence `≤ max 0 (deg A + 1)` when `h⁰(𝒪_X) = 1` (the geometrically-integral curve value,
    19	`ChiCurve.h0_moduleKSheaf`; kept as an explicit hypothesis here so the ledger layer stays
    20	on the abstract bundle).
    21	
    22	## Route (worksheet §5 DD-0: "peeling on the landed slice SES; base case via
    23	effective-witness degree ≥ 0")
    24	
    25	* **`h¹` never drops under effective twists** (`h1_add_single_le` →
    26	  `h1_add_effective_le`): the dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has
    27	  skyscraper cokernel with no `H¹`, so the slice machinery
    28	  (`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f`, `ChiSlice.lean`) gives a surjection
    29	  `H¹(𝒪(D − x)) ↠ H¹(𝒪(D))`; peel point by point exactly as `peel_effective`
    30	  (`FLVClass.lean`). In particular `h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪_X)` for `E ≥ 0`
    31	  (`h1_le_of_effective`).
    32	* **The effective witness** (`exists_effective_of_h0_pos`): a nonzero global section of
    33	  `𝒪(A)` is a rational function `g` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, an *effective* divisor of the
    34	  same class — the extraction of `exists_effective_of_picClass` run from `0 < h⁰`
    35	  directly (no Riemann inequality needed). This is the base case: `0 < h⁰ ⟹ deg A ≥ 0`.
    36	* **Assembly** (`h0_le_deg_add_h0_of_pos`, keystone `h0_divisorSheaf_le_max`): if
    37	  `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0`, replace `A` by the effective witness `E` (class-invariance of `h⁰` and
    38	  `deg`, `ClassCohomology`/`Degree`), then the χ-ledger `chi_divisorSheaf` reads
    39	  `h⁰(𝒪(E)) = χ(𝒪_X) + deg E + h¹(𝒪(E)) ≤ deg A + h⁰(𝒪_X)`.
    40	
    41	The `h¹`-monotonicity lemmas are exported (not private): F1's window comparisons reuse
    42	them, and they are the natural `H¹`-side companion of `peel_effective`.
    43	-/
    44

    62	
    63	/-- **The `h¹` dévissage step**: enlarging the divisor by a closed point can only shrink
    64	`h¹`: `h¹(𝒪(D)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(D − x))`. The dévissage SES `0 → 𝒪(D − x) → 𝒪(D) → sky → 0` has

    66	`Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` maps `H¹(𝒪(D − x))` onto `H¹(𝒪(D))`. -/
    67	theorem h1_le_h1_sub_single {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (D : X.CurveDivisor) :
    68	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K D)
    69	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by
    70	  haveI : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₃ 1) :=
    71	    skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one x (jumpModule K hx D)
    72	  haveI : Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ 1) :=
    73	    moduleFinite_hModule_divisorSheaf_one K (devissageDivisor hx D)
    74	  have hsurj : Function.Surjective (Sheaf.HModule.map (devissageSES K hx D).f 1) :=
    75	    Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f (devissageSES_shortExact K hx D) 1
    76	  have hle : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₂ ≤ Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₁ :=
    77	    LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_surjective hsurj
    78	  have hX₁ : Sheaf.h1 (devissageSES K hx D).X₁
    79	      = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (D - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) := by

    81	        = Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (devissageDivisor hx D)) := rfl
    82	    rw [h, devissageDivisor_eq_sub hx D]

    84	  rw [← hX₂, ← hX₁]

    87	/-- **Peeling one point on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(B + x)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(B))` — the additive form of the
    88	dévissage step. -/
    89	theorem h1_add_single_le {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (B : X.CurveDivisor) :
    90	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
    91	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K B) := by
    92	  have h := h1_le_h1_sub_single K hx (B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
    93	  have heq : B + CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 = B := by abel
    94	  rwa [heq] at h

    96	/-- **Peeling a multiple of a point on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(A + n·x)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(A))` — iterating
    97	`h1_add_single_le`. -/
    98	theorem h1_add_nsmul_single_le {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) (A : X.CurveDivisor)
    99	    (n : ℕ) :
   100	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1))
   101	      ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) := by
   102	  induction n with
   103	  | zero => simp
   104	  | succ n ih =>
   105	    have hstep := h1_add_single_le K hx (A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   106	    have heq : A + n • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 + CurveDivisor.single hx 1
   107	        = A + (n + 1) • CurveDivisor.single hx 1 := by
   108	      rw [succ_nsmul]; abel
   109	    rw [heq] at hstep
   110	    exact le_trans hstep ih

   112	/-- **Effective peeling on `h¹`**: `h¹(𝒪(A + E)) ≤ h¹(𝒪(A))` for any effective `E` —
   113	peel the finitely many points of `E` one multiplicity-block at a time, by induction on
   114	the size of the support (the `peel_effective` skeleton, `FLVClass.lean`). -/
   115	theorem h1_add_effective_le (A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E) :
   116	    Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) := by
   117	  suffices H : ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : X.CurveDivisor), 0 ≤ E →
   118	      (toFinsupp E).support.card = n →
   119	      Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K (A + E)) ≤ Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K A) from
   120	    H _ E hE rfl
   121	  intro n
   122	  induction n with
   123	  | zero =>
   124	    intro E hE hc
   125	    have hE0 : E = 0 :=
   126	      Finsupp.support_eq_empty.mp (Finset.card_eq_zero.mp hc)
   127	    rw [hE0, add_zero]
   128	  | succ n ih =>
   129	    intro E hE hc
   130	    classical
   131	    have hne : (toFinsupp E).support.Nonempty := by
   132	      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]; exact Nat.succ_pos n
   133	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hne
   134	    set b : ℤ := toFinsupp E p with hb
   135	    have hb_nonneg : 0 ≤ b := Finsupp.le_def.mp hE p
   136	    have hbpos : 0 < b := lt_of_le_of_ne hb_nonneg (Ne.symm (Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mp hp))
   137	    set E' : X.CurveDivisor := Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) with hE'
   138	    have hdecomp : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b + E' = E := by
   139	      rw [hE', hb]
   140	      exact Finsupp.single_add_erase p (toFinsupp E)
   141	    have hE'nonneg : 0 ≤ E' := by
   142	      rw [hE']
   143	      refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun q => ?_)
   144	      by_cases hq : q = p
   145	      · subst hq; rw [Finsupp.erase_same]; rfl
   146	      · rw [Finsupp.erase_ne hq]; exact Finsupp.le_def.mp hE q
   147	    have hcard : (toFinsupp E').support.card = n := by
   148	      have hEF : toFinsupp E' = Finsupp.erase p (toFinsupp E) := rfl
   149	      rw [hEF, Finsupp.support_erase, Finset.card_erase_of_mem hp, hc, Nat.succ_sub_one]
   150	    have hsingle : CurveDivisor.single p.2 b = b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   151	      rw [CurveDivisor.nsmul_single_one, Int.toNat_of_nonneg hb_nonneg]
   152	    have hsplit : A + E = (A + E') + b.toNat • CurveDivisor.single p.2 1 := by
   153	      rw [← hdecomp, ← hsingle]; abel
   154	    rw [hsplit]
   155	    exact le_trans (h1_add_nsmul_single_le K p.2 (A + E') b.toNat) (ih E' hE'nonneg hcard)

   159	theorem h1_le_of_effective (E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E) :

   161	  have h := h1_add_effective_le K 0 E hE

   166	
   167	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
   168	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (X.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
   169	/-- **An effective witness of any class with a nonzero section.** If `h⁰(𝒪(A)) > 0` then
   170	the class of `A` is realized by an **effective** divisor: a nonzero global section of
   171	`𝒪(A)` is `g ∈ K(X)ˣ` with `A + div g ≥ 0`, and that shift is effective of the same

   175	theorem exists_effective_of_h0_pos (A : X.CurveDivisor)
   176	    (hA : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K A)) :
   177	    ∃ E : X.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ E ∧ CurveDivisor.picClass K E = CurveDivisor.picClass K A := by

   183	    (isTerminalTop : IsTerminal (⊤ : X.Opens)) (X.divisorSheaf K A)) t with hs
   184	  have hsne : s ≠ 0 := by
   185	    rw [hs]; exact (LinearEquiv.map_ne_zero_iff _).mpr ht
   186	  set g : X.functionField := divisorVal K s with hg
   187	  have hgmem : g ∈ divisorSections K A ⊤ := divisorVal_mem K s
   188	  have hgne : g ≠ 0 := by
   189	    intro h
   190	    exact hsne (divisorSection_ext K
   191	      (show divisorVal K s = divisorVal K (0 : _) from by rw [← hg, h]; rfl))
   192	  -- the unit `u` and the effective shift.
   193	  set u : X.functionFieldˣ := Units.mk0 g hgne with hu
   194	  have huval : (u : X.functionField) = g := rfl
   195	  refine ⟨A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u, ?_, ?_⟩
   196	  · -- effectivity: `coeffAt (A + div u) ≥ 0` from the pole bound
   197	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
   198	    change (0 : ℤ) ≤ coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) u)

   200	    have hb := (mem_divisorSections_of_nonempty K htop).mp hgmem p.1 p.2 trivial
   201	    rw [← huval, Scheme.ord_val_eq K u p.2, divisorBound_le_iff p.2,
   202	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg] at hb
   203	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   204	    omega
   205	  · -- same class
   206	    rw [CurveDivisor.picClass_add, CurveDivisor.picClass_divOf, mul_one]

   221	  have hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K E = CurveDivisor.deg K A :=

   223	  have hchiE := chi_divisorSheaf K E

   227	      = (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K E) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.divisorSheaf K E) := rfl
   228	  have hchiO : Sheaf.chi (X.moduleKSheaf K)
   229	      = (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ) - Sheaf.h1 (X.moduleKSheaf K) := rfl

   235	theorem h0_divisorSheaf_le_max (A : X.CurveDivisor) :
   236	    (Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K A) : ℤ)
   237	      ≤ max 0 (CurveDivisor.deg K A + (Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) : ℤ)) := by
   238	  by_cases h : Sheaf.h0 (X.divisorSheaf K A) = 0

   241	  · exact le_max_of_le_right
   242	      (h0_le_deg_add_h0_of_pos K A (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h))
   243

   248	theorem h0_divisorSheaf_le_max_of_h0_one (hO : Sheaf.h0 (X.moduleKSheaf K) = 1)

     8	/-!
     9	# Rational points of a smooth curve over a separably closed field (DAT-P)
    10	
    11	The density brick **DAT-P** of the Wave-4 DATUM campaign (`informal/w4-datum-worksheet.md` §4
    12	DAT-P, §5 risk 4). Over a **separably closed** field `K`, the `K`-rational points of a scheme
    13	smooth of relative dimension `1` over `K` are dense: every nonempty open contains one.
    14	
    15	## Why smoothness is essential (and closed points are not enough)
    16	
    17	Over an imperfect separably closed field `K` (e.g. a separable closure of `𝔽ₚ(t)`) not every
    18	closed point is `K`-rational: `𝔸¹_K` has closed points with residue field `K(a^{1/p})`. So the
    19	algebraically-closed argument (`AlgebraicGeometry.pointEquivClosedPoint`, "every closed point is
    20	rational") **fails**. What survives is density of `K`-points, via the standard-smooth chart:
    21	
    22	* a standard-smooth chart of relative dimension `1` is étale over the affine line `𝔸¹`;
    23	* over the **infinite** field `K` a `K`-rational base point of `𝔸¹` lies under the chart;
    24	* the fibre there is a finite separable, indeed étale, `K`-algebra, which over the separably
    25	  closed `K` splits into copies of `K` — giving the rational point.
    26	
    27	The commutative-algebra core is `AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.SeparablyClosedFibre`
    28	(`AlgebraicGeometry.SeparablyClosed.exists_algHom_of_etale_mvPoly`); this file glues it to the
    29	scheme-level chart machinery of `SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1`.
    30	
    31	## Main results (`AlgebraicGeometry.SeparablyClosed`)
    32	
    33	* `exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one` — a **nonempty** scheme smooth of
    34	  relative dimension `1` over a separably closed field `K` has a `K`-point `Spec K ⟶ X` over `K`.
    35	* `exists_rationalPoint_mem` — **the keystone (density form).** For `f : X ⟶ Spec K` smooth of
    36	  relative dimension `1` over a separably closed `K` and any nonempty open `W` of `X`, there is a
    37	  `K`-point `p : Spec K ⟶ X` over `K` whose topological image lies in `W`. Instantiates at any
    38	  separably closed field of the standing curve pack (`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`) with
    39	  the open given as a nonempty open of the underlying space; consumed by DAT-B's coverage argument
    40	  (the P4(c) `h⁰`-drop with points at `kˢ`-levels).
    41	* `Over.exists_rationalPoint_mem` — the same, phrased for the standing pack `C : Over (Spec K)`.
    42	-/

    44	set_option autoImplicit false
    45	
    46	universe u
    47	
    48	open CategoryTheory AlgebraicGeometry MvPolynomial
    49	open scoped TensorProduct
    50	
    51	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.SeparablyClosed
    52	
    53	/-- **A nonempty smooth curve over a separably closed field has a rational point.** For a scheme
    54	`X` smooth of relative dimension `1` over a separably closed field `K`, if `X` is nonempty there is
    55	a `K`-point `p : Spec K ⟶ X` over `K` (`p ≫ f = 𝟙`).
    56	
    57	Proof: a standard-smooth chart `V ∋ x₀` of relative dimension `1` gives, via
    58	`RingHom.IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_etale_mvPolynomial` and transport across
    59	`Γ(Spec K, ⊤) ≅ K`, an étale `K[X]`-algebra structure on `Γ(X, V)`; the commutative-algebra core
    60	`exists_algHom_of_etale_mvPoly` yields a `K`-point `φ : Γ(X, V) →ₐ[K] K`, which `IsAffineOpen`
    61	machinery (`SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec`, `fromSpec_top`) turns into a `K`-point of `X` over `K`. -/
    62	theorem exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one {K : Type u} [Field K]
    63	    [IsSepClosed K] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f]
    64	    [Nonempty X] :
    65	    ∃ p : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X, p ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of K)) := by
    66	  obtain ⟨x₀⟩ := ‹Nonempty X›
    67	  obtain ⟨U, hU, V, hV, hx₀V, e, hsm⟩ :=
    68	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension.exists_isStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension (n := 1) (f := f) x₀
    69	  have hUtop : U = ⊤ := by
    70	    have hmem : f.base x₀ ∈ U := e hx₀V
    71	    ext y; simpa using Subsingleton.elim (f.base x₀) y ▸ hmem
    72	  subst hUtop
    73	  obtain ⟨g₀, hg₀C, hg₀E⟩ := hsm.exists_etale_mvPolynomial
    74	  letI e_K : Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), ⊤) ≃+* K :=
    75	    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
    76	  let g : MvPolynomial (Fin 1) K →+* Γ(X, V) :=
    77	    g₀.comp (MvPolynomial.mapEquiv (Fin 1) e_K.symm).toRingHom
    78	  have hgE : g.Etale :=
    79	    RingHom.Etale.stableUnderComposition _ _
    80	      (RingHom.Etale.of_bijective (MvPolynomial.mapEquiv (Fin 1) e_K.symm).bijective) hg₀E
    81	  letI algMP : Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) K) Γ(X, V) := g.toAlgebra
    82	  letI algK : Algebra K Γ(X, V) := (g.comp (MvPolynomial.C)).toAlgebra
    83	  haveI : Algebra.Etale (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) K) Γ(X, V) := by
    84	    rw [← RingHom.etale_algebraMap]; rwa [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    85	  haveI : IsScalarTower K (MvPolynomial (Fin 1) K) Γ(X, V) := by
    86	    apply IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq'
    87	    rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra, RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]; rfl
    88	  haveI : Nontrivial Γ(X, V) := PrimeSpectrum.nontrivial (hV.primeIdealOf ⟨x₀, hx₀V⟩)
    89	  obtain ⟨φ⟩ := SeparablyClosed.exists_algHom_of_etale_mvPoly (K := K) (S := Γ(X, V))
    90	  -- `(map e_K.symm) ∘ C = C ∘ e_K.symm`, hence the `K`-structure map factors the chart map
    91	  have hCmap : (MvPolynomial.mapEquiv (Fin 1) e_K.symm).toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.C) =
    92	      (MvPolynomial.C).comp e_K.symm.toRingHom := by
    93	    ext a
    94	    simp only [RingHom.comp_apply, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe, RingHom.coe_coe,
    95	      MvPolynomial.mapEquiv_apply, MvPolynomial.map_C]
    96	  have hI : (algebraMap K Γ(X, V)) = (f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom.comp e_K.symm.toRingHom := by
    97	    rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    98	    change (g₀.comp (MvPolynomial.mapEquiv (Fin 1) e_K.symm).toRingHom).comp MvPolynomial.C =
    99	      (f.appLE ⊤ V e).hom.comp e_K.symm.toRingHom
   100	    rw [RingHom.comp_assoc, hCmap, ← RingHom.comp_assoc, hg₀C]
   101	  -- the chart map post-composed with the `K`-point is the canonical iso `Γ(Spec K, ⊤) → K`
   102	  have hring : (f.appLE ⊤ V e) ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom =
   103	      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).hom := by
   104	    apply CommRingCat.hom_ext
   105	    have hφ : φ.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap K Γ(X, V)) = RingHom.id K := by
   106	      ext a; exact φ.commutes a
   107	    rw [hI, ← RingHom.comp_assoc] at hφ
   108	    have hthis := congrArg (fun r => r.comp e_K.toRingHom) hφ
   109	    simp only [RingHom.comp_assoc, RingEquiv.toRingHom_eq_coe, RingEquiv.symm_comp,
   110	      RingHom.comp_id, RingHom.id_comp] at hthis
   111	    rw [CommRingCat.hom_comp, CommRingCat.hom_ofHom]
   112	    exact hthis
   113	  refine ⟨Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ hV.fromSpec, ?_⟩
   114	  calc (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ hV.fromSpec) ≫ f
   115	      = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ (hV.fromSpec ≫ f) := by rw [Category.assoc]
   116	    _ = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫
   117	          (Spec.map (f.appLE ⊤ V e) ≫ hU.fromSpec) := by
   118	        rw [IsAffineOpen.SpecMap_appLE_fromSpec f hU hV e]
   119	    _ = Spec.map ((f.appLE ⊤ V e) ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom φ.toRingHom) ≫ hU.fromSpec := by
   120	        rw [← Spec.map_comp_assoc]
   121	    _ = Spec.map ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).hom) ≫ hU.fromSpec := by rw [hring]
   122	    _ = (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).toSpecΓ ≫ hU.fromSpec := by rw [SpecMap_ΓSpecIso_hom]
   123	    _ = 𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) := by
   124	        rw [show hU.fromSpec = (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)).isoSpec.inv from
   125	          IsAffineOpen.fromSpec_top]
   126	        exact Scheme.toSpecΓ_isoSpec_inv _
   127	
   128	/-- **DAT-P keystone (density form).** For a scheme `X` smooth of relative dimension `1` over a
   129	separably closed field `K` and any nonempty open `W ⊆ X`, there is a `K`-rational point
   130	`p : Spec K ⟶ X` over `K` whose topological image lies in `W`.
   131	
   132	Instantiate at any separably closed field of the standing curve pack by taking `f := C.hom`
   133	(`[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]`); the open `W` is a nonempty open of the underlying space.
   134	Consumed by DAT-B's coverage argument (the P4(c) `h⁰`-drop with points at `kˢ`-levels). -/
   135	theorem exists_rationalPoint_mem {K : Type u} [Field K] [IsSepClosed K] {X : Scheme.{u}}
   136	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] (W : X.Opens)
   137	    (hW : (W : Set X).Nonempty) :
   138	    ∃ p : Spec (.of K) ⟶ X, p ≫ f = 𝟙 (Spec (.of K)) ∧
   139	      p.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) ∈ W := by
   140	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (W.ι ≫ f) := IsZariskiLocalAtSource.comp ‹_› W.ι
   141	  haveI : Nonempty W.toScheme := by obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hW; exact ⟨⟨x, hx⟩⟩
   142	  obtain ⟨p', hp'⟩ := exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (W.ι ≫ f)
   143	  refine ⟨p' ≫ W.ι, ?_, ?_⟩
   144	  · rw [Category.assoc]; exact hp'
   145	  · simpa using (p'.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K)).2
   146	
   147	end AlgebraicGeometry.SeparablyClosed

   150	
   151	variable {K : Type u} [Field K]
   152	
   153	/-- **DAT-P keystone for the standing curve pack.** For the curve bundle `C : Over (Spec K)` smooth
   154	of relative dimension `1` over a separably closed field `K`, every nonempty open `W` of the
   155	underlying space `C.left` contains a `K`-rational point: a `K`-point `p : Spec K ⟶ C.left` over
   156	`K` whose topological image lies in `W`. -/
   157	theorem exists_rationalPoint_mem [IsSepClosed K] (C : Over (Spec (.of K)))
   158	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] (W : C.left.Opens) (hW : (W : Set C.left).Nonempty) :
   159	    ∃ p : Spec (.of K) ⟶ C.left, p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of K)) ∧
   160	      p.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) ∈ W :=
   161	  SeparablyClosed.exists_rationalPoint_mem C.hom W hW

    10	/-!
    11	# The fiber twist `Θₙ` of a finite map to the projective line
    12	
    13	For the curve bundle `Y` (integral, smooth of relative dimension one and quasi-compact over
    14	a field `K`) equipped with a **dominant** morphism `π : Y ⟶ ℙ¹`, this file pins the
    15	Wave-4 twist datum: the divisor class of `n · (fiber of π)` and its two-cover triviality
    16	*by construction*.
    17	
    18	## The fiber-divisor design decision
    19	
    20	The overlap of the pinned affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)` is the
    21	basic open of the **pulled-back chart-0 coordinate** `t₀ = π* (X₁/X₀) ∈ Γ(Y, V₀)`
    22	(`AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord`, the public re-derivation of the
    23	`private` lemma of `Cohomology.Finiteness`). The section `t₀` is regular on all of `V₀` —
    24	its germ at every point is a nonzero element of the domain stalk, since `t₀` is a unit at the
    25	generic point (`π` dominant) — and is a **unit exactly on the overlap** `V₀ ⊓ V₁`. Its zero
    26	locus on `V₀` is the fiber of `π` over the point `[1 : 0]` (where `X₁` vanishes).
    27	
    28	We therefore pin the fiber divisor of `Θₙ` as the local-equation system **on the pinned
    29	cover itself**: the equation `t₀ⁿ` on the chart `V₀` and the constant `1` on `V₁`. The
    30	transition cocycle between the two charts is then the two-cover unit cocycle
    31	`gₙ = t₀ⁿ|_{V₀ ⊓ V₁}` — trivial (a single global regular equation) on each chart by
    32	construction. This is the fiber-twist normalization certified in
    33	`informal/w4-datum-design.md` §2(a).
    34	
    35	## Main declarations
    36	
    37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberCoord` — the pulled-back chart-0 coordinate `t₀ ∈ Γ(Y, V₀)`.
    38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord` — the overlap is `Y.basicOpen t₀`
    39	  (public form of the `private` `Cohomology.Finiteness` seam).
    40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isUnit_fiberCoord_res_inf` — `t₀` restricts to a unit on the overlap:
    41	  the two-cover-unit-cocycle certificate.
    42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberDivisor` — the local-equation system `(t₀ⁿ on V₀, 1 on V₁)`
    43	  for `n · (fiber of π)`, a `Y.LocalEquations`.
    44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist` — the Picard class `Θₙ = 𝒪(n · fiber) = (fiberDivisor n).picClass`.
    45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist_succ`, `AlgebraicGeometry.fiberTwist_pow` — the twist is the
    46	  `n`-th power of the unit twist: `Θₙ = Θ₁ⁿ`.
    47	* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_fiberTwist` — the degree scales linearly,
    48	  `deg Θₙ = n · deg Θ₁` (the `= n · deg π` normalization is a *frontier*; see the note there).
    49	-/
    50

    53	applications) needs defeq checks through semireducible definitions, as in mathlib's own
    54	algebraic-geometry files. -/

    66	/-! ## The pinned cover and its local equations
    67	
    68	These constructions depend only on the morphism `π`; the integrality/smoothness hypotheses
    69	enter with the regularity of the equations in the next section. -/
    70	
    71	section Cover
    72	
    73	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ P1 K)
    74	
    75	/-- The standard grading of `K[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 K`. -/
    76	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) K
    77	
    78	/-- The chart-0 preimage `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`. -/
    79	@[reducible] noncomputable def fiberChart₀ : Y.Opens := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen K 0
    80	
    81	/-- The chart-1 preimage `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`. -/
    82	@[reducible] noncomputable def fiberChart₁ : Y.Opens := π ⁻¹ᵁ P1.chartOpen K 1
    83	
    84	/-- The **pulled-back chart-0 coordinate** `t₀ = π* (X₁/X₀) ∈ Γ(Y, V₀)`: the image under
    85	`π`'s section map of the chart-0 coordinate of `ℙ¹`. The two-cover overlap is the basic
    86	open of `t₀` (`preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord`), and its `n`-th power is the twist's
    87	transition cocycle. -/
    88	noncomputable def fiberCoord : Γ(Y, fiberChart₀ π) :=
    89	  (π.app (P1.chartOpen K 0)).hom ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord K 0 1))
    90	
    91	/-- **The two-cover overlap is the basic open of `t₀`.** Public re-derivation of the
    92	`private` lemma `Cohomology.Finiteness.preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_left`: the overlap of the
    93	pinned chart preimages equals `Y.basicOpen t₀`, obtained from `Scheme.preimage_basicOpen`
    94	together with the `ℙ¹`-side identification `P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord`. -/
    95	theorem preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord :
    96	    fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π = Y.basicOpen (fiberCoord π) := by
    97	  have h : π ⁻¹ᵁ ((P1 K).basicOpen
    98	        ((Proj.awayToSection 𝒜 (X 0)).hom (P1.chartCoord K 0 1)))
    99	      = Y.basicOpen (fiberCoord π) :=
   100	    Scheme.preimage_basicOpen π _
   101	  rw [P1.basicOpen_awayToSection_chartCoord K 0 1, Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf] at h
   102	  exact h
   103	
   104	open Classical in
   105	/-- The pinned two-chart pointed cover: `V₀` at every point of `V₀`, `V₁` elsewhere. -/
   106	noncomputable def fiberCover : Y.PointedCover where
   107	  opens z := if z ∈ fiberChart₀ π then fiberChart₀ π else fiberChart₁ π
   108	  mem_opens z := by
   109	    by_cases h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π
   110	    · rw [if_pos h]; exact h
   111	    · rw [if_neg h]
   112	      have hz : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π ⊔ fiberChart₁ π := by
   113	        rw [preimage_chartOpen_sup]; trivial
   114	      exact (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup.mp hz).resolve_left h
   115	
   116	lemma fiberCover_opens_of_mem {z : Y} (h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π) :
   117	    (fiberCover π).opens z = fiberChart₀ π :=
   118	  if_pos h
   119	
   120	lemma fiberCover_opens_of_notMem {z : Y} (h : z ∉ fiberChart₀ π) :
   121	    (fiberCover π).opens z = fiberChart₁ π :=
   122	  if_neg h
   123	
   124	open Classical in
   125	/-- The local equation of `n · (fiber)` at a point: `t₀ⁿ` on the chart `V₀`, the constant
   126	`1` on `V₁`. -/
   127	noncomputable def fiberEqn (n : ℕ) (z : Y) : Γ(Y, (fiberCover π).opens z) :=
   128	  if h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π then
   129	    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_of_eq (fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h))).op).hom
   130	      ((fiberCoord π) ^ n)
   131	  else 1
   132	
   133	lemma fiberEqn_of_mem (n : ℕ) {z : Y} (h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π) :
   134	    fiberEqn π n z
   135	      = (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_of_eq (fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h))).op).hom
   136	          ((fiberCoord π) ^ n) :=
   137	  dif_pos h
   138	
   139	lemma fiberEqn_of_notMem (n : ℕ) {z : Y} (h : z ∉ fiberChart₀ π) :
   140	    fiberEqn π n z = 1 :=
   141	  dif_neg h
   142	
   143	/-- The fiber equation is multiplicative in the exponent: `t₀^(n+1) = t₀ⁿ · t₀`. This is the
   144	section-level heart of the power law `Θₙ = Θ₁ⁿ`. -/
   145	lemma fiberEqn_succ (n : ℕ) (z : Y) :
   146	    fiberEqn π (n + 1) z = fiberEqn π n z * fiberEqn π 1 z := by
   147	  by_cases h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π
   148	  · rw [fiberEqn_of_mem π (n + 1) h, fiberEqn_of_mem π n h, fiberEqn_of_mem π 1 h,
   149	      ← map_mul, pow_one, ← pow_succ]
   150	  · rw [fiberEqn_of_notMem π (n + 1) h, fiberEqn_of_notMem π n h, fiberEqn_of_notMem π 1 h,
   151	      one_mul]
   152	
   153	/-- The zeroth fiber equation is the constant `1`. -/
   154	lemma fiberEqn_zero (z : Y) : fiberEqn π 0 z = 1 := by
   155	  by_cases h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π
   156	  · rw [fiberEqn_of_mem π 0 h, pow_zero, map_one]
   157	  · rw [fiberEqn_of_notMem π 0 h]
   158	
   159	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
   160	private lemma res_comp {W V U : Y.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(Y, U)) :
   161	    (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
   162	      = (Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
   163	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
   164	
   165	/-- **The two-cover-unit-cocycle certificate.** The restriction of `t₀` to the overlap
   166	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` is a unit: every point of the overlap lies in `Y.basicOpen t₀`. Hence `t₀ⁿ` is a
   167	genuine unit Čech cocycle on the pinned two-cover. -/
   168	theorem isUnit_fiberCoord_res_inf :
   169	    IsUnit ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE
   170	        (inf_le_left : fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π ≤ fiberChart₀ π)).op).hom
   171	      (fiberCoord π)) := by
   172	  apply Y.toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
   173	  intro w hw
   174	  rw [Y.presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   175	  refine (Y.mem_basicOpen (fiberCoord π) w hw.1).mp ?_
   176	  rw [← preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord π]
   177	  exact hw
   178	
   179	end Cover
   180	
   181	/-! ## Regularity and the fiber divisor -/
   182	
   183	section Main
   184	
   185	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
   186	  (π : Y ⟶ P1 K) [IsDominant π]
   187	
   188	/-- The standard grading of `K[X₀, X₁]`, the graded ring underlying `P1 K`. -/
   189	local notation "𝒜" => homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) K
   190	
   191	/-- The generic point of `Y` lies in the two-cover overlap: since `π` is dominant, the
   192	`ℙ¹`-overlap `D₊(X₀X₁)` (nonempty as the range of its affine chart) meets the range of `π`,
   193	so its `π`-preimage is a nonempty open of the irreducible `Y`. -/
   194	theorem genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf :
   195	    genericPoint Y ∈ fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π := by
   196	  have hP1 : (↑(P1.chartOpen K 0 ⊓ P1.chartOpen K 1) : Set (P1 K)).Nonempty := by
   197	    rw [P1.chartOpen_inf]
   198	    obtain ⟨z⟩ : Nonempty (Spec (CommRingCat.of
   199	        (Away 𝒜 ((X 0 : MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K) * X 1)))) := inferInstance
   200	    refine ⟨(Proj.awayι 𝒜 _ (P1.X_mul_X_mem K) two_pos).base z, ?_⟩
   201	    rw [← Proj.opensRange_awayι 𝒜 _ (P1.X_mul_X_mem K) two_pos]
   202	    exact ⟨z, rfl⟩
   203	  have hne : (↑(π ⁻¹ᵁ (P1.chartOpen K 0 ⊓ P1.chartOpen K 1)) : Set Y).Nonempty := by
   204	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ :=
   205	      π.denseRange.inter_open_nonempty _ (P1.chartOpen K 0 ⊓ P1.chartOpen K 1).isOpen hP1
   206	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hp.2
   207	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
   208	    change π.base y ∈ (P1.chartOpen K 0 ⊓ P1.chartOpen K 1 : (P1 K).Opens)
   209	    rw [(hy : π.base y = p)]
   210	    exact hp.1
   211	  rw [← Scheme.Hom.preimage_inf]
   212	  exact genericPoint_mem_of_nonempty hne
   213	
   214	/-- The germ of the pulled-back coordinate at any point of `V₀` is nonzero: it maps, under
   215	the domain stalk's embedding into the function field, to the germ at `η`, which is a **unit**
   216	(the generic point lies in `Y.basicOpen t₀`). -/
   217	theorem germ_fiberCoord_ne_zero {y : Y} (hy : y ∈ fiberChart₀ π) :
   218	    (Y.presheaf.germ (fiberChart₀ π) y hy).hom (fiberCoord π) ≠ 0 := by
   219	  have hη : genericPoint Y ∈ fiberChart₀ π := (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).1
   220	  have hunit : IsUnit ((Y.presheaf.germ (fiberChart₀ π) (genericPoint Y) hη).hom
   221	      (fiberCoord π)) := by
   222	    refine (Y.mem_basicOpen (fiberCoord π) (genericPoint Y) hη).mp ?_
   223	    rw [← preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord π]
   224	    exact genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π
   225	  intro hzero
   226	  have key := germ_generic_eq_algebraMap_germ (X := Y) hη hy (fiberCoord π)
   227	  rw [hzero, map_zero] at key
   228	  rw [key] at hunit
   229	  exact not_isUnit_zero hunit
   230	
   231	/-- The germ of `t₀` at a point of `V₀` is a nonzerodivisor of the domain stalk. -/
   232	theorem germ_fiberCoord_mem_nonZeroDivisors {y : Y} (hy : y ∈ fiberChart₀ π) :
   233	    (Y.presheaf.germ (fiberChart₀ π) y hy).hom (fiberCoord π)
   234	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors (Y.presheaf.stalk y) :=
   235	  mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mpr (germ_fiberCoord_ne_zero π hy)
   236	
   237	/-- **The fiber divisor `n · (fiber of π)`.** The local-equation system on the pinned
   238	two-cover: `t₀ⁿ` on `V₀` (regular everywhere, vanishing to order `n` on the fiber over
   239	`[1 : 0]`) and `1` on `V₁`. The overlap ratio is the unit `t₀ⁿ`. -/
   240	noncomputable def fiberDivisor (n : ℕ) : Y.LocalEquations where
   241	  cover := fiberCover π
   242	  eqn := fiberEqn π n
   243	  regular z y hy := by
   244	    by_cases h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π
   245	    · rw [fiberEqn_of_mem π n h, Y.presheaf.germ_res_apply, map_pow]
   246	      exact pow_mem (germ_fiberCoord_mem_nonZeroDivisors π _) n
   247	    · rw [fiberEqn_of_notMem π n h, map_one]
   248	      exact one_mem _
   249	  ratio_isUnit z z' := by
   250	    by_cases h : z ∈ fiberChart₀ π <;> by_cases h' : z' ∈ fiberChart₀ π
   251	    · refine ⟨1, ?_⟩
   252	      rw [Units.val_one, one_mul, fiberEqn_of_mem π n h, fiberEqn_of_mem π n h',
   253	        res_comp, res_comp]
   254	    · have hle : (fiberCover π).opens z ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens z' ≤ fiberChart₀ π :=
   255	        inf_le_left.trans (le_of_eq (fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h))
   256	      have hbo : ∀ w ∈ (fiberCover π).opens z ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens z',
   257	          w ∈ Y.basicOpen (fiberCoord π) := by
   258	        intro w hw
   259	        rw [← preimage_inf_eq_basicOpen_fiberCoord π]
   260	        exact ⟨(fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h) ▸ hw.1,
   261	          (fiberCover_opens_of_notMem π h') ▸ hw.2⟩
   262	      have hunit : IsUnit ((Y.presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op).hom ((fiberCoord π) ^ n)) := by
   263	        apply Y.toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
   264	        intro w hw
   265	        rw [Y.presheaf.germ_res_apply, map_pow]
   266	        exact ((Y.mem_basicOpen (fiberCoord π) w (hle hw)).mp (hbo w hw)).pow n
   267	      refine ⟨hunit.unit, ?_⟩
   268	      rw [fiberEqn_of_notMem π n h', map_one, mul_one, IsUnit.unit_spec,
   269	        fiberEqn_of_mem π n h, res_comp]
   270	    · have hle : (fiberCover π).opens z ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens z' ≤ fiberChart₀ π :=
   271	        inf_le_right.trans (le_of_eq (fiberCover_opens_of_mem π h'))
   272	      have hbo : ∀ w ∈ (fiberCover π).opens z ⊓ (fiberCover π).opens z',
   273	          w ∈ Y.basicOpen (fiberCoord π) := by
   274	        intro w hw

   115	/-- **The θ-family is multiplicative in its class.** -/
   116	theorem thetaFamily_mul (L L' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic)
   117	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   118	    thetaFamily C (L * L') T = thetaFamily C L T * thetaFamily C L' T := by

   123	/-- **The θ-family sends inverses to inverses.** -/

   125	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   126	    thetaFamily C L⁻¹ T = (thetaFamily C L T)⁻¹ := by

   135	    (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (m : ℕ) :
   136	    thetaFamily C (L ^ m) T = thetaFamily C L T ^ m := by
   137	  unfold thetaFamily thetaBase
   138	  rw [map_pow, map_pow, map_pow, map_pow]

   153	/-- **The chart twist is ONE θ-family** (this file's headline).

   180	    (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic :=

   209	/-- **A presenting datum for the collapsed twist class exists**, over any affine base and for

   211	
   212	`c` here is the honest Čech class of the plus class being tested (over the étale carrier,

   216	theorem exists_datum_cechPicClass_chartTwistClass {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]

   218	    (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor) :
   219	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
   220	      D.cechPicClass
   221	        = c * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k B) (chartTwistClass C m Z) :=
   222	  BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq _

    83	construction that never mentions the Abel chart), while `V = ⊤` returns the unrestricted
    84	certificate that three headers call false.  So any workable `V` is a proper intermediate open,
    85	CHART-U(b)'s openness is load-bearing, and the pair `(huniv V, hcov V)` has **no measured
    86	inhabitant at any `V`** (`I-1012`).  Two bad endpoints are two refutations, not a non-vacuity
    87	check.
    88	
    89	## Main declarations
    90	
    91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine` — **the site fact**, with no
    92	  presheaf and no chart: a sieve on `T` is covering as soon as its pullback along every map
    93	  from an affine scheme in a cover of `T` is covering.
    94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal` — **the reduction**: pointwise
    95	  coverage over affine tests only gives `ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
    96	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine` — the composite with B-6, i.e.
    97	  the instance `pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test data alone.
    98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally` — the converse, so the affine form
    99	  is not a strengthening.
   100	-/

   102	set_option autoImplicit false
   103	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
   104	
   105	universe u
   106	
   107	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
   108	
   109	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
   110	
   111	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   112	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   113	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   114	
   115	noncomputable section
   116	
   117	/-! ## The site fact -/
   118	
   119	/-- **A sieve is covering as soon as it is covering after pullback to affine pieces.**
   120	
   121	Stated for an arbitrary sieve on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses.  The
   122	cover is `Scheme.affineCover`, whose members are affine by
   123	`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`, and the deduction is `GrothendieckTopology.transitive`
   124	against the presieve the cover generates.
   125	
   126	This is the step the coverage chain was missing: it says the Zariski-local-surjectivity
   127	obligation may be discharged one affine piece of the test at a time. -/
   128	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine {T : Scheme.{u}} (S : Sieve T)
   129	    (h : ∀ (j : T.affineCover.I₀), S.pullback (T.affineCover.f j) ∈
   130	      Scheme.zariskiTopology (T.affineCover.X j)) :
   131	    S ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
   132	  have hcov : (Sieve.generate (Presieve.ofArrows T.affineCover.X T.affineCover.f))
   133	      ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T :=
   134	    Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr ⟨T.affineCover, Sieve.le_generate _⟩
   135	  refine Scheme.zariskiTopology.transitive hcov S ?_
   136	  rintro Y g ⟨V, a, b, ⟨j⟩, rfl⟩
   137	  rw [Sieve.pullback_comp]
   138	  exact Scheme.zariskiTopology.pullback_stable a (h j)
   139	
   140	/-! ## The reduction -/
   141	
   142	variable (C) in
   143	/-- **THE AFFINE-TEST REDUCTION**: pointwise coverage over affine tests gives
   144	`ChartsCoverLocally` at every test.
   145	
   146	The hypothesis is `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise`'s, with `[IsAffine Y]` added and
   147	nothing else changed.  So a coverage producer may assume its test is affine — hence, through
   148	`divFamZarAffineEquiv`, that its divisor data lives over a *ring*, which is where every
   149	producer in this project is stated. -/
   150	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   151	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   152	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   153	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   154	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   155	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   156	  intro T s
   157	  refine mem_zariskiTopology_of_pullback_affine _ fun j => ?_
   158	  -- the pullback of the supremum is the supremum of the pullbacks, and each is the image
   159	  -- sieve of the RESTRICTED section — so the obligation at the affine piece is exactly the
   160	  -- affine instance of the hypothesis
   161	  have hpb : (⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i) s).pullback (T.affineCover.f j)
   162	      = ⨆ i, Presheaf.imageSieve (f i)
   163	          ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s) := by
   164	    -- `Sieve.pullback` preserves `iSup` (it is a left adjoint), and per index it turns the
   165	    -- image sieve of `s` into that of `s` restricted along the cover map
   166	    simp only [← Presheaf.pullback_imageSieve]
   167	    ext Y g
   168	    simp only [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply, Sieve.pullback_apply]
   169	    aesop
   170	  rw [hpb]
   171	  -- the piece is affine (`Scheme.isAffine_affineCover`), so the hypothesis applies AT IT — note
   172	  -- `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` cannot be cited here, since it quantifies over all tests
   173	  -- and would demand the datum at the non-affine ones too; the site bridge is what is reused
   174	  choose W hW i x hx using h (T.affineCover.X j)
   175	    ((pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (T.affineCover.f j).op s)
   176	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun y => ⟨x y, hx y⟩
   177	
   178	variable (C) in
   179	/-- **B-5 over affine tests ⟹ B-6**: the local-surjectivity instance
   180	`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts` consumes, from affine-test coverage data alone. -/
   181	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_affine {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   182	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   183	    (h : ∀ (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y] (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) (y : ↥Y),
   184	      ∃ (W : Y.Opens) (_ : y ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   185	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   186	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   187	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_affineLocal C f h)
   188	
   189	/-! ## The converse -/
   190	
   191	variable (C) in
   192	/-- **The affine form is not a strengthening**: `ChartsCoverLocally` gives back, over each
   193	affine test, a cover on whose members some chart hits the section.
   194	
   195	Read the carrier honestly, exactly as `pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally` does: the sieve
   196	condition returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with open-immersion maps, not by opens of
   197	the test, so the converse produces a cover map where the hypothesis consumed an opens
   198	inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — that the affine-only hypothesis is available, not
   199	chosen for provability — a cover map is exactly as good. -/
   200	theorem affineLocal_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   201	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   202	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (Y : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine Y]
   203	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op Y)) :
   204	    ∃ (𝒰 : Y.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   205	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   206	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s :=
   207	  pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally C f h Y s
   208	
   209	end
   210	
   211	end AlgebraicGeometry

    71	noncomputable section
    72	
    73	/-! ## The bridge, with no chart content
    74	
    75	Stated for an arbitrary family of sieves on an arbitrary scheme, because that is all it uses:
    76	the coverage half of B-5 is a statement about the *site*, and mixing it with the presheaf
    77	statement is what made it look gated. -/
    78	
    79	/-- **Pointwise data gives a covering supremum sieve.**
    80	
    81	If every point `t` of `T` has an open neighbourhood `W t` and an index `idx t` such that the
    82	inclusion `(W t).ι` lies in the `idx t`-th sieve, then the supremum of the family is a
    83	Zariski covering sieve of `T`.
    84	
    85	The proof is the cover `{W t}_{t : ↥T}` — jointly surjective because `t ∈ W t`, open
    86	immersions because they are opens inclusions — fed to `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`, and
    87	then `le_iSup` at the index of the destructed point.
    88	
    89	Note there is **no compatibility condition between different points**: `idx` is an arbitrary
    90	function.  That is why chart-parameter heterogeneity (dat-b row, `Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree`)
    91	costs nothing here — a supremum sieve never asks its members to agree. -/
    92	theorem mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {T : Scheme.{u}}
    93	    (Sv : ι → Sieve T) (W : ↥T → T.Opens) (hW : ∀ t, t ∈ W t) (idx : ↥T → ι)
    94	    (hmem : ∀ t, (Sv (idx t)).arrows (W t).ι) :
    95	    (⨆ i, Sv i) ∈ Scheme.zariskiTopology T := by
    96	  refine Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mpr
    97	    ⟨Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers (↥T) (fun t => (W t : Scheme.{u})) (fun t => (W t).ι)
    98	      (fun t => ⟨t, ⟨t, hW t⟩, rfl⟩) (fun t => inferInstance), ?_⟩
    99	  rintro V g ⟨t⟩
   100	  exact le_iSup Sv (idx t) _ (hmem t)
   101	
   102	/-! ## `ChartsCoverLocally` from what B-5 actually produces -/
   103	
   104	variable (C) in
   105	/-- **THE B-5 PACKAGING**: `ChartsCoverLocally` from pointwise coverage.
   106	
   107	The hypothesis is exactly the shape the coverage geometry delivers, and is worth reading
   108	field by field against `w4-datb` §1.2.  For every test `T`, every degree-zero class `s` on
   109	it, and every point `t` of `T`:
   110	
   111	* `W` — an open neighbourhood of `t`.  In the intended instantiation this is
   112	  `chartLocusOpens` (`Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean`), whose openness is CHART-U(b) and is
   113	  unconditional since `IsSplitWitnessIsoInvariant` was discharged;
   114	* `i` — the chart index, chosen *at `t`*.  Per-point by construction, which is what the
   115	  I-0204 non-uniformity of the twist exponent `m` requires;
   116	* `x` — a point of the `i`-th chart scheme over `W`, i.e. the divisor family the coverage
   117	  argument produces at the splitting field of `κ(t)`;
   118	* `hx` — that its class is `s` restricted to `W`.
   119	
   120	Given that, the sieve condition holds.  So a coverage lane never has to mention `Sigma.desc`,
   121	a coproduct of yoneda presheaves, a covering sieve, or a Grothendieck topology: it produces
   122	four things at a point and this lemma does the rest.
   123	
   124	**What this does not do.**  It does not produce the pointwise data — that is B-5's geometry
   125	and its residue (the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation) is recorded on the dat-b row.
   126	It removes the site-theoretic layer between that geometry and B-6, which had never been
   127	written down and which the row described as though it were already there. -/
   128	theorem chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   129	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   130	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   131	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   132	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   133	    ChartsCoverLocally C f := by
   134	  intro T s
   135	  choose W hW i x hx using h T s
   136	  exact mem_zariskiTopology_iSup_of_pointwise _ W hW i fun t => ⟨x t, hx t⟩
   137	
   138	variable (C) in
   139	/-- **B-5 ⟹ B-6 in one step**: pointwise coverage gives the local-surjectivity instance.
   140	
   141	The composite of `chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise` with `isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc`.
   142	Recorded because it is the statement a lane closing coverage wants to cite: the *only*
   143	remaining input to the `[Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f)]`
   144	instance that three files carry as an unproduced `variable` is the pointwise data above. -/
   145	theorem isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   146	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   147	    (h : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) (t : ↥T),
   148	      ∃ (W : T.Opens) (_ : t ∈ W) (i : ι) (x : (W : Scheme.{u}) ⟶ X i),
   149	        (f i).app (op (W : Scheme.{u})) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (W.ι).op s) :
   150	    Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology (Sigma.desc f) :=
   151	  isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc f (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise C f h)
   152	
   153	/-! ## The converse: the pointwise form is not a strengthening
   154	
   155	A reduction whose hypothesis is strictly stronger than its conclusion is a weakening in
   156	disguise, and the memory `reduction-needs-its-converse` is about exactly this failure.  Here
   157	the converse holds — modulo the one difference that is genuinely there and is named. -/
   158	
   159	variable (C) in
   160	/-- **`ChartsCoverLocally` gives back an open cover on whose members a chart hits `s`.**
   161	
   162	The converse direction, and the check that the pointwise hypothesis above is the right one.
   163	From the sieve condition one extracts a Zariski cover of `T` by `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff`
   164	and reads the supremum membership at each cover map.
   165	
   166	**The one honest difference**, and it is why this is stated with a general `Y ⟶ T` rather than
   167	an open of `T`: `mem_grothendieckTopology_iff` returns a cover by *arbitrary* schemes with
   168	open-immersion maps, not by opens of `T`.  Those are the same up to isomorphism
   169	(`Scheme.Hom.isoOpensRange`) but not on the nose, so the converse produces a cover map where
   170	the hypothesis consumed an opens inclusion.  For the purpose this serves — showing the
   171	pointwise data is *available*, hence not a hypothesis chosen for provability — a cover map is
   172	exactly as good, and pretending otherwise would need a transport that adds nothing. -/
   173	theorem pointwise_of_chartsCoverLocally {ι : Type u} {X : ι → Scheme.{u}}
   174	    (f : ∀ i, yoneda.obj (X i) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1)
   175	    (h : ChartsCoverLocally C f) (T : Scheme.{u})
   176	    (s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T)) :
   177	    ∃ (𝒰 : T.Cover.{u} (Scheme.precoverage @IsOpenImmersion)),
   178	      ∀ j : 𝒰.I₀, ∃ (i : ι) (x : 𝒰.X j ⟶ X i),
   179	        (f i).app (op (𝒰.X j)) x = (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.map (𝒰.f j).op s := by
   180	  obtain ⟨𝒰, hle⟩ := Scheme.mem_grothendieckTopology_iff.mp (h T s)
   181	  refine ⟨𝒰, fun j => ?_⟩
   182	  have hj := hle (𝒰.X j) (𝒰.f j) (Presieve.ofArrows.mk j)
   183	  rw [iSup, Sieve.sSup_apply] at hj
   184	  obtain ⟨S, ⟨i, rfl⟩, x, hx⟩ := hj
   185	  exact ⟨i, x, hx⟩
   186	
   187	end
   188	
   189	end AlgebraicGeometry
